question: According to the GOLD guidelines, which post-bronchodilator spirometric criterion confirms the diagnosis of COPD?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The GOLD criterion for COPD is a fixed post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio < 0.70, regardless of predicted values.
Incorrect. A reduced FEV1% predicted indicates severity (GOLD 2 = 50–79%), but the diagnostic criterion is the FEV1/FVC ratio < 0.70.
Incorrect. FVC reduction suggests a restrictive pattern. COPD is diagnosed by an obstructive pattern: FEV1/FVC < 0.70.
Incorrect. The GOLD threshold is < 0.70 (70%), not 0.80. Values of 0.70–0.80 are borderline and may represent normal ageing.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the GOLD diagnostic criteria: COPD is confirmed by a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio < 0.70.
Well done. The GOLD fixed-ratio criterion (FEV1/FVC < 0.70 post-bronchodilator) is the cornerstone of COPD diagnosis.
